column1: # The conformance table for naming an agent identity.
# One recogniser is written twice, in shell (`lib/attribution.sh`, read by review
# sweeps) and in Rust (the `message-attribution` lint in `mockspace-extra-lints`),
# and the two must not drift. This file is what both suites read: the lists the
# recogniser is built from, and the people and agents it must tell apart. A row
# changed here fails whichever implementation disagrees, and an implementation
# changed without a row fails its own suite.
# Format: `kind<TAB>value`. Blank lines and lines opening with `#` are ignored.
# The recogniser reads what only an agent carries, in this order:
#   marker     a bot marker, matched anywhere in the name or the mailbox;
#   mailbox    a mailbox an agent commits from, a glob over the whole mailbox
#              (`*` stands for any run of characters);
#   tool       a tool's own name, which is an agent's only as the whole of a name:
#              optionally behind `head` words, optionally followed by `companion`
#              words and versions (a word opening with a digit, or `v` and digits)
#              and nothing else. The words are those of the name, lowercased and
#              split at anything that is not a letter or a digit;
#   given      a tool whose name is also somebody's given name. It counts as a
#              tool only with a second signal: a head word, a companion or version
#              after it, or one of the mailboxes above;
#   head       a vendor word allowed in front of a tool's name;
#   companion  a word allowed after a tool's name: a model, a product, a surface.
# A group in parentheses is read on its own: when it is a tool's name the identity
# is an agent's (`Jane Smith (aider)`), and otherwise it is left out
# Below the lists come the verdicts: `person` rows are never an agent, `agent` rows
# always are, as an author, a committer and the value of a `Co-Authored-By`.
